To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
detection of tyrosine mRNA by RT– PCR is not an independent predictor of short-term recurrence in patients with melanoma.
the presence of tyrosinise mRNA in sentinel lymph nodes of patients with melanoma does not predict short-term recurrence of the disease.
the detection of melanoma-specific mRNA in the sentinel nodes of melanoma is not an independent predictor of recurrence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular mechanisms involved in the development of melanoma.
the development of an effective and safe treatment for malignant melanoma, the deadliest form of skin cancer.
the detection of tyrosine mRNA by RT-PCR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the detection of tyrosine mRNA in sentinel lymph nodes of patients with cutaneus melanoma, in the absence of metastases on routine histopathological examination (HISNEG /PCRPOS), does not predict short-term disease recurrence.
tyrosinase RT-PCR is not a predictor for short-term disease recurrence in patients with melanoma.
the presence of tyrosinasespecific mRNA in the sentinel node is not a predictor for short-term disease recurrence in patients with melanoma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of tyrosinise mRNA in sentinel nodes is not a significant predictor of short-term recurrence.
tyrosinase RT–PCR is an unreliable predictor for recurrence in the setting of negative histopathologic evaluation.
tyrosinase RT–PCR positivity is not predictive of recurrence in patients with histologically negative sentinel lymph nodes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RT-PCR is not a predictor for short-term disease recurrence in the absence of a histologic finding.

detection of tyrosine mRNA in the sentinel nodes of melanoma patient’s lymph nodes by RT–PCR is not a predictor for short-term disease recurrence, and the detection of capsular nevi in the lymph nodes of melanomas patients is also not a predictor for disease recurrence.
the presence of capsular nevi in sentinel lymph nodes does not appear to be a predictor of recurrence.
